subject: Pulser Health trial: environment decisioning, success criteria & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@pulserhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jay Patel <j.patel@pulserhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pulser Health - trial environment options and success criteria

Thanks for the call this morning — Alex from Pulser Health here. Quick recap and asks so we have a single source of truth. Appreciate the time from the Redwood team.

Call summary (participants: Alex, Jay (IT), Sean (Redwood), Marissa (Redwood - commercial), Rishi (Redwood SE)):
- Objective: validate Redwood inference for embedded charting and clinical summarization for our patient messaging pipeline.
- Primary non-functional concerns: data residency (US-only), encryption at rest (KMS/HSM), and deterministic latency for 95th pctile.

Customer success criteria (what will make the trial a win):
1) Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for 256-token prompts during peak test (simulated 50 req/s).
2) Throughput: sustained 40–60 inference QPS without queueing spikes for 10-minute ramp.
3) Quality: F1 on named-entity extraction & hallucination rate < 2% across our 300 sample prompts.
4) Security: VPC connectivity or equivalent network isolation + support for our KMS policies.
5) Cost: projected per-1000-token unit cost that keeps monthly inference spend < $15k at expected volume.

What we want from Redwood:
- Recommended trial path (hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC) with pros/cons and expected timelines.
- Network & firewall requirements to share with our infra team.
- A minimal test plan we can run that maps to the success criteria above (metrics to capture + sample dataset ingestion).
- Estimate of any trial credits / discount for the POC and rough cost for dedicated sandbox & VPC staging.

Timeline proposals:
- Kickoff: week of May 3 (we can do a short runbook review + initial account setup).
- Quick smoke test (hosted) within 72 hours of kickoff.
- Dedicated perf run 7–10 days after smoke (if needed).
- VPC readiness: depend on our infra availability — ideally parallel prep but we can prioritize hosted path first.

Attachments: pulser_trial_success_criteria.xlsx (sample prompts & scoring), network_requirements_pulser.pdf

Open questions from our side:
- Can hosted be configured to honor our retention/KMS requirements for the smoke test?
- If we do hosted first, how do you help us validate p95 latency under realistic traffic?

Next steps: please confirm owners, the recommended path, and any dates you need from our infra/legal.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Head of Product, Pulser Health

---
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@pulserhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Jay Patel <j.patel@pulserhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pulser Health - trial environment options and success criteria

Alex — great notes, thanks for pulling these together. Below is a concretized plan and recommended path based on Pulser's success criteria. I also included owners and what we need to unblock each phase.

High-level recommendation (sequence):
1) Hosted smoke (fastest path, 48–72h): validate model outputs and baseline latency/quality on a small controlled test harness. Pros: immediate onboarding, no infra work. Cons: limited control over KMS/retention.
2) Dedicated sandbox perf (1 week): provision a dedicated GPU pool we control and run the throughput/latency ramp. Pros: predictable performance at scale, tuning/quantization options. Cons: provisioning lead time and cost.
3) VPC trial (parallel prep, 1–3 weeks): for compliance: VPC + customer-managed KMS. This is the full-compliance path Pulser expects; we can start network prep in parallel with hosted smoke.

Mapping to your success criteria:
- Latency/Throughput: Dedicated sandbox run (step 2) is where we will demonstrate p95 under load. We’ll provide a perf harness and run with your sample prompts.
- Quality: Hosted smoke will give quick signal; then we’ll lock prompts and run the formal evaluation on dedicated. We’ll deliver a short evaluation report with our scoring.
- Security/KMS: Hosted cannot meet full KMS/HSM integration for keys you control. For smoke, we can isolate data and honor retention settings, but VPC + customer KMS is the only option for full compliance.
- Cost: I’ll ask Marissa for a trial credit and short estimate for dedicated sandbox and VPC monthly run rates.

Owners & immediate asks:
- Trial lead (Redwood): Sean Gallagher — overall coordination, perf runs, and runbook execution.
- Commercial/credits: Marissa Cole — credit/discount and procurement coordination.
- SE/engineering: Rishi Malhotra — perf tuning, network checklist, run harness.
- Pulser owners: Alex (product) and Jay (infra) — confirm desired test window + provide an allowlist for IP blocks.

Proposed near-term timeline (aggressive):
- May 3: Kickoff + runbook review (30–45min).
- May 5–7: Hosted smoke (we’ll provision access and run sample prompts).
- May 10–17: Dedicated sandbox perf window (if smoke looks good).
- Parallel: VPC network prep — Jay to share firewall rules and KMS requirements; we will provide VPC onboarding guide.

Deliverables we’ll provide:
- Perf harness + run script (captures p50/p95/qps, errors)
- Evaluation report with quality scoring against your spreadsheet
- Network checklist & VPC onboarding playbook
- Short cost estimate for expected monthly volumes

Attachments / links: trial runbook (Drive) and HubSpot deal created: https://hubspot.com/deals/12345

Action items (for the next 48h):
- Alex/Jay: confirm May 3 kickoff availability (morning PT preferred) and share a small set (<= 300) of representative prompts.
- Jay: share firewall/egress IP allowlist or tell us if you want us to open an ingress peer.
- Marissa: can you confirm if we can offer $5k trial credit for Pulser?

I’ll follow up with calendar invites and a short runbook link.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: pulser_trial_success_criteria.xlsx (received), network_requirements_pulser.pdf

---
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@pulserhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jay Patel <j.patel@pulserhealth.com>, Chris Long <chris.long@pulserhealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pulser Health - trial environment options and success criteria

Thanks Sean — that sequence makes sense and aligns with our risk profile. We’ll do the hosted smoke first to get output quality checked and then run the perf on a dedicated sandbox. A few clarifications:

- For the hosted smoke: we will need confirmation that data used in the smoke will not be retained beyond the test window and that logs can be scoped to only the evaluation prompts. Is that possible?
- KMS: for the hosted smoke we can use redacted data; we’ll only pursue full KMS integration if the perf results justify moving to VPC.
- Cost ask: please include an estimate showing the delta in monthly run cost between hosted and dedicated sandbox for 200k tokens/day.

Availability: May 3 kickoff at 10:00 AM PT works for our team. Jay will share our infra allowlist by EOD today.

Also cc’ing our procurement lead (Chris) — Chris, we’ll probably need a short path to PO for dedicated sandbox if we move forward quickly.

Thanks,
Alex
